title: MinHash-driven prompt deduplication and cache compaction
creator: Evelyn Zhang
description:
Background: Our GPU-resident KV cache stores prefixes/prompt contexts across requests to accelerate autoregressive decoding. As request diversity grows (multi-tenant workloads, chat sessions, templated prompts), the cache contains many near-duplicate entries that occupy precious GPU memory and reduce effective residency for hot sequences.

Proposal summary: Introduce a MinHash-based similarity index for online deduplication and compaction of prefix entries. Instead of relying only on exact fingerprinting, we compute lightweight MinHash signatures per prefix segment (configurable k-shingles) at admission time and maintain a compact in-GPU index of signatures. For high-similarity hits (>= configurable threshold), we merge references and store a canonicalized representation with a narrow delta overlay. This yields lower duplicate token-residency, better batch hit rates across interleaved workloads, and modest compute overhead compatible with continuous batching.

Key ideas: compute 64-bit MinHash sketches on host at batching boundary; keep a small GPU-resident lookup table mapping sketch->canonical fragment id; if similarity above threshold, create an overlay delta stored in host memory and small pointer in GPU cache; incremental compaction job scavenges low-use variants and compacts them into canonical fragments; admission policy favors exact-match fast path but falls back to similarity probe for space-limited pools.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads
Prototype integrated into staging serving runtime for one model type (e.g., LLaMA-2-13B)
End-to-end tests validate correctness of returned tokens when canonicalization+delta overlay applied
Measured GPU KV memory occupancy reduction of at least 18% on representative multi-tenant trace
No regression >5% in median P50 token latency for steady-state traffic; tail P99 increase <=10% during compaction windows
Feature gated and rollout plan documented; safe rollback pathway implemented
implementation_notes: MinHash sketch uses 8 independent hashes over 8-token shingles; stored as 64-bit combined sketch for compactness

Admission flow: compute sketch on CPU while forming microbatch; before GPU upload, probe GPU sketch table; if hit, check delta size; if delta <= 32 bytes use overlay path, else fall back to full upload
Compact index layout: vector of (sketch, fragment_id, refcount) packed to 64B alignment; index can be sharded by GPU slot for lockless updates
Compaction: background task runs per-GPU at low priority, merging low-refcount variants into canonical chunk and updating pointers atomically
Fallbacks: disable similarity probe for dedicated-capacity customers in first rollout if requested; expose feature flag per-tenant
test_plan: Unit tests for MinHash sketch correctness and collision profile over synthetic prompt families
Integration tests verifying token stream equivalence for canonicalized vs original prefixes
Load test on staging using 10M request trace (multi-tenant) to measure occupancy, hit-rate, latencies
Chaos test: force compaction mid-batch and validate in-flight request correctness and recovery
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic with A/B metrics tracked (latency, cost per token, cache hit-rate)
benchmarks: Initial sim on representative trace: duplicate cluster reduction 24%, expected GPU-resident prefix slots freed ~19%
Microbenchmark: sketch compute adds ~6-12us per request on host CPU per 1k-token window; amortized in microbatching
End-to-end staging run: P50 token latency change +2.1%, P99 +7.8% during compaction sweeps
Estimated token-cost reduction: 6-9% for chat workloads with templated prompts
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and tenant opt-in metadata
Phase 1: internal staging for model family and internal tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 2: canary 5% hosted traffic, monitor metrics for 48 hours
Phase 3: expand to 25% with adaptive compaction thresholds, remediate regressions
Phase 4: global rollout with tenant opt-out and explicit dedicated/enterprise exclusion options
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: MinHash collisions could incorrectly merge semantically different prefixes -> Mitigation: conservative similarity threshold (0.85) and delta-size limit; safety validation in integration tests
Risk: extra CPU overhead during microbatching -> Mitigation: sketch computed at batching boundary and vectorized; fall back to exact-only policy for low-latency SKUs
Risk: compaction sweep causes transient latency spikes -> Mitigation: background throttling, cooperative compaction windows aligned with low-load periods
Risk: complexity increases debugging surface -> Mitigation: add verbose telemetry for sketch probes, merge events, and delta sizes; build replay tools
notes_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-421234 (microbatch boundary refactor), ENG-412007 (gpu-index-sharding)
Follow-up: consider integrating locality-sensitive hashing for long-sequence workloads if MinHash overhead too high
